question: Should OpenClaw use the shared `notificationWake.reactions` policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical opt-in reaction-turn contract, or choose a narrower/per-message design instead?
rationale: The issue requests new user-facing wake/config semantics across multiple channels, and current open PRs implement overlapping API shapes that automation should not pick without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt Shared Policy
options.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best PR candidate with docs, generated config metadata, and channel tests.

options.title: Narrow By Channel
options.body: Start with one channel-specific implementation such as Discord or Telegram, accepting that cross-channel semantics may need a later unification pass.

options.title: Defer Reaction Wakes
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and close or pause the open implementation PRs until maintainers want this config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Policy
recommendation.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best PR candidate with docs, generated config metadata, and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the open shared-policy candidate and has recent history in the reaction, system-event, and heartbeat wake paths.
